title: Swin Transformer for Fast MRI
grouping: Four panels with black dashed rounded outlines, each titled at the top left with a letter and one word: (A) Challenge and (B) Solution share the top row as equal halves; (C) Overview of SwinMR takes the wider bottom-left; (D) Results the narrower bottom-right. The panels tell a story: problem, idea, method, outcome.
shapes_depth: (A) and (B) draw receptive fields on a sagittal brain MRI: a small coloured square for a convolution kernel, a red frame over a white patch grid for full self-attention, red window frames for windowed attention and translucent red bands for shifted windows. (C) draws the network as flat trapezoids (IM, OM) flanking a wide rectangle (FEM) in muted blue-violet, data as MRI thumbnails (ZF, Recon, GT), multi-coil ground truth as an offset deck, the mask as a black tile with vertical white lines and sensitivity maps as a small grey stack; the losses are math (L_pixel, L_freq, L_VGG) reached by arrows labelled FFT and VGG, with footnote marks * and ** explained at the bottom. (D) is a 2 x 2 grid of result thumbnails, each with a red zoom box and an enlarged inset in its lower-left corner.
proposed_highlight: The method is named in panel (C)'s title and under its network; in the results grid it takes the last tile.
lesson: Use Figure 1 as a four-panel story - challenge, solution, method, results - in lettered dashed panels, and state the problem on the actual scan (kernel and window extents drawn as coloured squares and grids over a brain MRI) rather than on abstract tokens.
notes: Venue from the PDF (Neurocomputing); year = arXiv preprint year (2201.03230). The figure is embedded in the PDF as one raster image, so photo_share is unknown (null) and the palette is measured over the whole raster.

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)

core.what: a four-panel story in reading order inside dashed rounded frames: (A) Challenge and (B) Solution across the top, (C) Overview of SwinMR widened at bottom left, (D) Results at bottom right

relations.form: panels lettered A to D in a 2 x 2 grid; inside (C) a zero-filled image passes left to right through a blue IM-FEM-OM hourglass to a reconstruction, with a skip line arching over the network
(A) and (B) draw four attention schemes on the same sagittal MR slice side by side (Conv2D, MSA, W-MSA, SW-MSA); (D) is a 2 x 2 grid of GT, ZF, DAGAN and SwinMR with matching zoomed insets
receptive fields and windows are drawn as red and blue boxes and grids directly on the MR image; the undersampling mask is drawn as vertical stripes and the coil data as a stack of channel images
in (C) the reconstruction and the multi-channel ground truth are both wired into three loss symbols (L_pixel, L_freq via FFT, L_VGG via VGG) placed between them in the lower right
in (D) a red box on each image is enlarged as an inset at its lower left

channels.colour: images are greyscale; red = window or receptive-field boundaries in (A)/(B) and also the zoom boxes and insets in (D), so red carries two meanings; blue square = the query region in (A)/(B) and muted blue = the network in (C)
channels.shape: MR slices = data; a trapezoid-rectangle-trapezoid hourglass = the network; stacked slices = multi-channel data; L symbols = losses
channels.line: solid arrows for both data flow and loss inputs; operations (FFT, VGG, the mask) are labels on arrows; asterisks on arrows point to footnotes (root sum square, k-space undersampling)
channels.frame: a dashed rounded frame = one lettered panel

quality.strengths: Every data element is a real MR image, and the attention windows are drawn on the image itself, so the motivation (local vs global vs shifted windows) is visible; the losses are drawn as separate terms with the operation that feeds each (FFT, VGG) on its arrow.
quality.weaknesses: In (C) the loss wiring is tangled: lines from Recon and from the multi-channel GT run down and across to three stacked L symbols, a sensitivity-map stack sits in the middle with a short curved arrow, and footnote asterisks carry meaning; the network itself is one undifferentiated hourglass while motivation and results take three of the four panels; red means both 'window' and 'zoom region'.

insights.structure: A 2x2 grid of dashed rounded panels lettered (A) Challenge, (B) Solution, (C) Overview of SwinMR, (D) Results; (C) is widened to hold the network and losses, (D) is a 2x2 image grid.
insights.data: Every data element is a real sagittal brain MR slice (ZF, GT, Recon, multi-channel GT stack, sensitivity maps, mask stripes); attention windows are drawn as red/blue grids directly on the MR image in (A)/(B).
insights.emphasis: The network is one hourglass (IM - FEM - OM) in muted blue at top of (C); results panel (D) puts red zoom insets on each reconstruction so SwinMR vs DAGAN differences show at a glance.
insights.flow: Panels read like text, A->B on top then C->D; inside (C) ZF goes right through SwinMR to Recon, then three losses (L_pixel, L_freq, L_VGG) gather at the bottom-right fed by arrows labelled FFT and VGG from Recon and GT.
insights.avoid: Loss arrows in (C) cross each other and the footnote markers (*, **) push key operations (RSS, k-space undersampling) into tiny footnotes instead of labelled boxes.

arrangement.units: four dashed rounded panels in a 2x2 grid, each titled with a letter and name at its top-left
arrangement.inputs_as: real zero-filled MR image (ZF) and GT at the left edge of panel (C)
